newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Jan platinum imports surge on Russian news.
newsitem.headline: Japan Jan platinum imports surge on Russian news.

text.p: Japan's imports of platinum group metals surged in January as local traders boosted spot-market purchases because of an expected delay in Japan-Russia export talks, the traders said on Friday.

Japan's palladium imports in January jumped 224 percent from a year earlier to 8.15 tonnes, while platinum imports in the same month rose by 63.6 percent to 7.1 tonnes from the previous year, Finance Ministry data released on Friday showed.
"Because we expected Japan-Russia platinum group metal export talks to be delayed, we have stepped up our spot-market buying since the end of last year," an official of a major bullion house said.
The Russian platinum group metal agency informed Japanese traders in December that their regular export negotiations would be postponed due to Russian budget problems.
Traders said the jump in imports was solely due to news of the delay in trade talks, and not because of increased demand.

Although the figures showed that Russian platinum imports were at relatively normal levels of 1.17 tonnes for platinum and 5.418 tonnes for palladium in January, traders said the imports largely consisted of metals of Russian origin which were imported from third countries.
Traders said imports of platinum group metals were likely to have remained at high levels in February.

"Imports of platinum group metals in February are likely to be high, as lingering uncertainty over the Japan-Russia talks has forced us to cover metals in the spot-market," a trading house trader said.

Annual Japan-Russia talks on platinum group metals, which are usually held in mid-December, have been postponed indefinitely due to problems with the Russian budget and other domestic factors, and there have been no Russian shipments so far this year.
